Case built for teaching: the underlying CT is real (public archive) and has no lesions; the lesions were added by computer with the noise of the original image. The realism is good but simplified: no histology, the outcome is the one set in the simulation.
Hematogenous lung metastases are typically multiple, round, sharply marginated nodules of different sizes (seeded at different times), predominantly at the bases and in the periphery, where more blood flows. In colorectal cancer the lung is the second site after the liver (especially in rectal cancer, because of systemic venous drainage).
Reading: count and measure at least the target nodules (RECIST 1.1: up to 2 per organ, ≥ 10 mm), compare with prior CTs. The Fleischner guidelines do not apply to oncologic patients.
Trovato un nodulo, cerca il secondo: nel: Found one nodule, look for the second: in the oncologic patient, multiple round nodules at the bases = metastases until proven otherwise.
Caso simulato: 8 noduli aggiunti al comp: Simulated case: 8 nodules added by computer (5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 13 and 15 mm). No histology.
Metastasi polmonari in un controllo onco: Lung metastases on an oncologic follow-up: this is what the follow-up looks for; the requesting physician reads them in the report. A documented communication is acceptable if it immediately changes therapy.
